<description>
**Problem:** Setting up an encrypted connection derives six values with the same secret. Each HKDF expansion repeats two SHA256 compressions to hash the same HMAC key pads.

**Fix:** Hash the key pads once per HKDF context, then copy the prepared HMAC state for each expansion. The copy replaces two setup compressions, saving ten SHA256 compressions across the six outputs - the derived bytes stay identical. [RFC 2104 section 4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2104.html#section-4) describes this optimization:

[quoted text omitted]

```text
BIP324_HKDF (ops/s, higher is better)
Before  █████████████████████████████████░░░░░░░  1,430,064  (baseline)
After   ████████████████████████████████████████  1,724,373  (+20.6%)
```
</description>

<commits>
448ac7bcef crypto: require a fixed-size HKDF output buffer

The array parameter decays to a pointer, so callers can supply fewer than 32 writable bytes without a compiler diagnostic.
Take a fixed-size byte span and pass output containers directly so their sizes are checked at compile time.

1cda969466 refactor: extract HKDF key setup

Extract key setup into PrepareHMAC before reusing prepared HMAC state.
Pass input key material as a byte span so callers can use their existing byte containers directly.

d1d1409d17 test, bench: cover repeated HKDF expansion

Check fixed outputs for all six BIP324 labels and interleaved reuse of the existing HKDF test vectors.
Measure HKDF context creation, the six BIP324 expansions, and clearing together before reusing prepared HMAC states.

80130b90e2 crypto: copy HMAC state instead of rehashing key pads

Each HKDF expansion hashes the same two HMAC key pads, costing two SHA256 compressions before hashing the label.
Prepare those states once per HKDF context and replace the repeated hashing with a copy of the prepared HMAC state.
Across BIP324's six expansions this saves ten SHA256 compressions, with identical derived bytes.
Cleanse the temporary extracted secret after constructing the prepared state.
</commits>
